source: Flashlight Emitter Reference — Lumens, CRI, Candela & Throw.md

W1.title: W1 (CSLNM1.TG)
W1.notes: 1 mm² die, cool white (~6000K). Unmatched pencil-beam throw for its size. The same package also comes in red, green, verdure, orange and blue (see §7).

SFT-25R.title: SFT-25R

candela.beam: Tiny intense hotspot; ~2× W1's lumens, slightly less intensity

SFT-25R.notes: 5000K, 5700K or 6500K (samples run cooler than nominal), plus a 5700K 90 CRI WG version. Small round die (about half the SFT-40's area) = extreme throw; out-throws the SFT-40 in the same host. Standard 3535 footprint fits most EDC/thrower boards.

W2.title: W2 (CSLPM1.TG)
W2.notes: 2 mm² die; white is 5700K only, and the same package also comes in green and deep blue (see §7). Handles more current than W1 for a wider, brighter hotspot.

SFT-40.title: SFT-40

candela.beam: Best all-round thrower hotspot (more usable spill than SFT-25R)

SFT-40.notes: Domeless all-round thrower king: punchy hotspot with usable spill. 6500K leans green, 5000K is decent, and 3000K is the high-CRI version.

SFT-42R.title: SFT-42R

candela.beam: Fatter, higher-lumen hotspot; comes into its own in large reflectors

SFT-42R.notes: 5000–6500K. Round-die thrower with a bigger hotspot than SFT-40 and ~2 A more draw. Best in large reflectors (Convoy L21B); in TIR or small hosts it throws less than the SFT-40. Phosphor is more brittle than other SFT parts, so don't let a TIR press on it.

SFT-60.title: SFT-60

candela.beam: Fatter, higher-lumen hotspot; comes into its own in large reflectors

SFT-60.notes: 5000K/5700K/6500K, 6.0 mm² die, 15 A max. High Vf (~3.3 V @ 10 A, ~3.5 V @ 15 A per one user), so a single-cell buck driver may not reach full current. Sits between SFT-40 and SFT-90.

SBT90.2.title: SBT90.2

candela.beam: Wall of light and long throw. These big dies are a poor match for 35–40 mm reflectors and need 60 mm+ to peak

SBT90.2.notes: Monster throw + lumens (~5700K). Expensive and power-hungry (~20 A+), greenish on low modes.

SFT-90.title: SFT-90 (bin code SFT-90X…)

candela.beam: Wall of light and long throw. These big dies are a poor match for 35–40 mm reflectors and need 60 mm+ to peak

SFT-90.notes: 6500K only; a pre-production sample measured green (Duv +0.007). Much cheaper alternative to the SBT90.2 with slightly lower performance. High Vf at high current makes FET/direct-drive and 1-cell buck drivers a poor match.

F150R.title: F150R (Convoy)

candela.beam: Wall of light and long throw. These big dies are a poor match for 35–40 mm reflectors and need 60 mm+ to peak

F150R.notes: Rated to 30 A. Convoy says it sits on or below the Planckian locus (no green push). Users report the 4000K as nicely negative-Duv but the 3000K as slightly green. Fits 21700 hosts such as the M21H.

SFT-70.title: SFT-70
SFT-70.notes: Domeless SST-70; efficient boost/buck-driven thrower. Convoy lists four bins with CRI from 70 to 95. Users rate the 3000K 95 CRI version's tint very highly.

FFL505A.title: FFL505A (FireflyLite)
FFL505A.notes: Small round die (2.35 mm²) under glass, ringed by brittle white silicone. Same chip as the LMP W5050SQ3, so it's a Lumenpioneer part. Relatively high luminance for a warm high-CRI LED, but very inefficient: 31 lm/W at max, "probably the most inefficient modern 5050" the tester has measured. An SFT-40 3000K matches its throw at ~6 A. A 6500K / 97 CRI version also exists.

XHP50.3 HI.title: XHP50.3 HI
XHP50.3 HI.notes: ANSI bins 3000K–7000K plus EasyWhite 2700K–4000K. Compact quad-die workhorse; very efficient with decent throw, though tint can be a lottery.

NTG50.title: NTG50 (Noctigon / Hank)
NTG50.footprint: 5050 · 6V (XHP50 footprint and voltage, so a drop-in for 6V XHP50.3 HI). 12V needs a different MCPCB
NTG50.output: ~2,100–3,300 lm (no lab test yet). Max ~8 A (listing)
NTG50.colour: 1800K / 2700K / 4200K / 5000K, ~95 CRI. Hank's charts show Duv ~−0.006 to −0.010
NTG50.notes: Hank's high-CRI XHP50.3 HI alternative: similar cd/lm, slightly fewer lumens. Hank says a neutral version isn't planned because "we need to guarantee that the tint is on the rosy side". Maker undisclosed.

SFN60.title: SFN60
SFN60.notes: Common Emisar / Noctigon hotrod emitter. Decent tint at 6500K, slightly green at 5500K. Competes with the SBT90 on lumens but throws less. Not sold bare by Convoy, but still offered in the Noctigon KR1 and Lumintop D3 (Nov 2026).

519A.title: 519A
519A.notes: The all-round gold standard. Wide range of CCTs (Convoy sells 1800K–5700K), neutral to rosy tint. Floody with the dome on. Easily dedomed for more throw, a lower CCT and a rosier tint. "V1" is the newer, preferred revision.

FFL351A.title: FFL351A (FireflyLite)
FFL351A.notes: Domeless flip-chip, ~2 × 2 mm chip, 4.3 mm² glowing area. Beam looks like a dedomed 519A with a slightly larger corona. Efficiency gains flatten above ~5 A. A newer run is reportedly less rosy than early batches. CCTs range from 1800K to 5000K. In a 7-emitter light it beat a domed 519A by only ~3% in lumens, with negligible extra throw.

XHP70.3 HI.title: XHP70.3 HI
XHP70.3 HI.notes: The go-to for high sustained output. ANSI bins 3000K–7000K plus EasyWhite 2700K–4000K. Domeless HI (3.9 mm source) roughly doubles intensity and cleans up the beam vs domed HD (5.3 mm source; 4,857 / 6,405 lm).

FFL707A.title: FFL707A (FireflyLite)
FFL707A.colour: "4000K" sample: 4277K, Ra 89, R9 49, Duv −0.016 (claimed −0.001). Another sample: Ra 97–98 (Opple meter)
FFL707A.notes: Four dies in the XHP70.3 HI footprint, but wired differently, so it needs its own board. Less flux and luminance than XHP70.3 HI. The gaps between dies can show a "donut hole" in smooth reflectors. ~9 A is the sensible limit. Samples vary a lot.

LHP73B.title: LMP LHP73B
LHP73B.notes: 1800K, 3000K, 4000K, 5000K or 6500K. High-power 3V flood/general-purpose competitor to XHP70.3 HI, with higher sustained output in Convoy lights.

219.title: 219B
219.notes: Legendary rosy tint (especially the sw45k 4500K bin). Low output and dislikes high current; largely replaced by 519A / NTG35.

219C.title: 219C
219C.notes: Sold in 3000K, 3500K, 4000K, 5000K and 5700K. The brighter but less-talented successor to the 219B; itself largely superseded by the SST-20 and LH351D.

219F.title: 219F
219F.notes: Successor to the 219C; best known for an 1800K sodium-lamp-like version. Doesn't like being overdriven.

B35AM.title: B35AM
B35AM.notes: Four tiny dies with a natural, sunlight-like tint. R9080 bins span 2700K–6500K. Its odd footprint needs a dedicated MCPCB, which limits overdrive.

719A.title: 719A
719A.notes: Flat (domeless) emitter with two stacked dies, usually sold in 4000K or 5000K. Colour like a dedomed 519A with more output but a floodier beam; generally considered underwhelming.

144A.title: 144A
144A.notes: Nichia's answer to the XHP50 (different footprint, no thermal pad). High CRI but strong tint shift without diffusion; used in the Armytek Wizard C2 Pro Nichia, which is 4500K.

E21A.title: E21A / E17A
E21A.notes: Ultra-high CRI, usually used in quads or larger arrays. 1850K–6500K, plus specialty colours such as E17A Azure.

E17A.title: E21A / E17A
E17A.notes: Ultra-high CRI, usually used in quads or larger arrays. 1850K–6500K, plus specialty colours such as E17A Azure.

SFT-12.title: SFT-12
SFT-12.notes: About half the SFT-25R's emitting area (6500K). Tight pencil beam, but at the same current the SFT-25R is much brighter and throws further.

SST-20.title: SST-20
SST-20.notes: Budget domed emitter. The ≤4000K high-CRI version is R9080; 5000K–6500K is bright but notoriously green on low. Also sold as SST-20-DR 660 nm deep red.

SST-40.title: SST-40 / SST-70
SST-40.notes: SST-40: 5000K, 5700K or 6500K. SST-70: 5700K or 6500K. Domed, cheap, high-output flood/hybrid LEDs common in budget lights; very green at low power.

SST-70.title: SST-40 / SST-70
SST-70.notes: SST-40: 5000K, 5700K or 6500K. SST-70: 5700K or 6500K. Domed, cheap, high-output flood/hybrid LEDs common in budget lights; very green at low power.

XHP35.title: XHP35.2 HI
XHP35.notes: Domeless 3535 multi-die. The older 12V XHP35 HI (discontinued) is still sought after for its 4000K tint.

XP-L HI.title: XP-L HI
XP-L HI.notes: 2700K–6500K by order code; Convoy sells 3000K, 4000K, 5000K and 6500K. Classic domeless EDC emitter; mostly superseded by 519A, SFT-40 and NTG35.

XP-G3.title: XP-G4 / XP-L2
XP-G3.notes: Both 2700K–7000K. Efficient and very common in mainstream brands (Fenix, Olight, etc.). Domed, with poor colour and noticeable tint shift; enthusiasts generally avoid them.

XP-G2.title: XP-G2
XP-G2.notes: 2700K–6500K. The tiny-die classic for micro quads and triples, now largely displaced by the XP-G3/G4. Smaller dome and die than the XP-L, with correspondingly less output.

XM-L2.title: XM-L2
XM-L2.notes: 2700K–7000K. The classic budget flooder, redesigned in 2021 as a flip chip ("the XM-L3 that never was"): much more efficient, lower Vf, and it survives ~17 A in overdrive tests. Same XM footprint, so existing boards and centering rings still fit. Luminance is only XP-L HD class and dedoming gains <10%, so it's a flood LED, not a thrower.

XHP50.2.title: XHP50.2 / XHP70.2
XHP50.2.notes: ANSI bins 3000K–7000K, EasyWhite 2700K–5000K. Older domed XHP generation: very bright but floody, with visible rainbow tint shift. Still sold by Convoy.

XHP70.2.title: XHP50.2 / XHP70.2
XHP70.2.notes: ANSI bins 3000K–7000K, EasyWhite 2700K–5000K. Older domed XHP generation: very bright but floody, with visible rainbow tint shift. Still sold by Convoy.

Boost HX.title: Boost HX (CULPM1.TG)
Boost HX.notes: Cool white: the datasheet's typical colour point (x 0.32, y 0.33) is about 6000K, and Convoy sells it as 6500K. 2 mm²-class die in the bigger Oslon Boost package, which runs cooler and takes more overdrive. Common in Convoy throwers (S21B, M21-series).

P9.title: P9 (GW PUSTA1.PM)
P9.notes: Flashlight versions are 5700K or 6500K (datasheet range 2200K–6500K). Domed, mainly cool white; competes with the XP-L HD in budget/mainstream lights. Poor colour rendering.

F45R.title: F45R (Convoy)
F45R.notes: 10 A max. 3000K/4000K/5000K. A user described it as "a cross between an SFT40 and an SFT60".

SFQ-55.title: SFQ-55
SFQ-55.notes: Listed at 5000K. San'an's 3V XHP50.3 HI competitor; high CCT with a clean cool tint. Now on its 4th generation.

SFQ-60.title: SFQ-60
SFQ-60.notes: Nightwatch sells its SFQ-60 lights at 5500K. Competes with the XHP50 at a lower Vf; very high CCT with a clean tint.

SFN-43.title: SFN-43
SFN-43.notes: Extremely bright 5050 that competes with the XHP50.2; very high CCT (≈6000K).

SFN-55.2.title: SFN-55.2
SFN-55.2.notes: Sold as cool white only; San'an parts like this usually come in 6500–7000K. Nine-die 7070 that sits between the XHP70.2 and the SBT90.2 in size and output; large colour variation with power level and generally greenish tint.

SFH-43.title: SFH-43
SFH-43.notes: Very bright with more throw than the SFH-55; dead neutral tint.

SFH-55.title: SFH-55
SFH-55.notes: Nominal 6500K; one lab sample measured 7413K, Duv −0.0004. Huge domeless 16-die LED, easily swapped with the SBT90.2; brighter but less throwy.

SFP-55.title: SFP-55
SFP-55.output: 22,000 lm claimed · ~15,000 lm measured in a light

SFY-55.title: SFY-55
SFY-55.notes: Also 6500K 70 CRI (lab: 5954K, Ra 69, Duv +0.007). 64-die monster emitter; gigantic footprint makes it very niche.

FFL909A.title: FFL909A (FireflyLite)
FFL909A.footprint: 9090 · listed as 3V (36 A max), but a near-identical part tests as ~9V
FFL909A.notes: 36 chips (the tested part was 3S × 12P). Listing claims 100 W, with 5000K Ra70 / 4000K Ra95 / 1800K Ra90 options. Very large emitting area (~71 mm²) means flood only, no throw. Possibly made by Hopthink. The FFL909MX variant (T9R, E90) is reported as brighter but greener.

NTG35.title: NTG35 (Noctigon / Hank)
NTG35.output: In a Noctigon D4V2 quad: ~2,900 lm OTF (4200K/5000K), 2,500 (2700K), 2,000 (1800K), Hank's figures. Measured ~2,900 lm turbo in a KR3 triple
NTG35.colour: Listed: 1800K Ra 92; 2700K / 4200K / 5000K Ra 95. Measured in lights: 2700K Ra 97, Duv −0.004; 4200K Ra 98, Duv −0.006 to −0.010
NTG35.notes: Hank's house high-CRI 3535, "free of greenish tint". Maker and construction undisclosed. Users find it rosier than a 219B (sometimes too rosy). Floody beam (~3.8 cd/lm in a KR3 triple). Main rivals: FFL351A, 519A.

FFL5009R.title: FFL5009R (FireflyLite)
FFL5009R.notes: Domeless quad-die "HI" part sold loose in 1800K / 2700K / 4000K / 5000K, plus a rosy 3500K in some lights. The listing gives Duv ±0.0005 for the original 4800–5300K bin. One reviewer reports Ra 95 / R9 97 for the 3500K L50 Sol, with no method stated. It's probably related to the Hopthink FL5009R that koef3 tested (3V, 11.8 mm² glowing area, 3,564 lm @ 20 A at 25 °C, Ra 94, R9 99, Duv −0.002, measured ~5900K). That test found a throwy all-rounder beam, but with a yellowish spot in smooth reflectors.

FFL5009D.title: FFL5009D (FireflyLite)
FFL5009D.notes: Domed version of the FFL5009R, with a wider, smoother beam and less throw (170–190 m vs 175–220 m in the same light). 3000K (rosy) / 4000K / 5000K. Only sold in lights.

FFL350RD.title: FFL350RD (FireflyLite)
FFL350RD.notes: Sold as a 3500K "round die", but the test found an ordinary rectangular flip chip masked to look round. Measured 4024K with Duv +0.001, not the listed 3500K on-BBL tint. The tester advises staying below 5–6 A: after a few minutes at 8.2 A the part changed (flux up >60%, tint much cooler) and later measured below 90 CRI. Out of stock.

FFL350DD.title: FFL350DD (FireflyLite)
FFL350DD.output: ~710–790 lm each (claimed 8,500–9,500 lm from 12 in the E12 Eclipse)
FFL350DD.notes: FireflyLite calls it "a big upgrade" on the FFL350RD: a round die with high CRI and better throw. 5700K and 3700K (slightly rosy). Only sold in lights; no test yet.

FFL505HB.title: FFL505HB (FireflyLite)
FFL505HB.output: ~1,300 lm each (claimed 5,200 lm from four in the E04 Surge)
FFL505HB.notes: Cool white 6000–6500K. Claimed to throw further than the quad FFL505A in the same light (650 m vs 480 m). Only sold in lights.

FFL707MD.title: FFL707MD (FireflyLite)
FFL707MD.notes: Round-die high-CRI 7070, 4200K with a slightly rosy tint. Claimed ~480 m in the X1S Pharos reflector version.

FFL707MX.title: FFL707MX (FireflyLite)
FFL707MX.notes: 5500K high-output thrower option, claimed at 1,080 m vs 915 m for the SBT90.2 option in the same light. The E90 page also introduces a 9090 round-die FFL909MX and a high-CRI round-die FFL707RD.

LHP531.title: LMP LHP531
LHP531.notes: 1800K–6500K (1800K is PC-amber style). Very cheap with a clean multi-die beam and slightly rosy 3000K–5000K tint.

W5050SQ3.title: LMP W5050SQ3
W5050SQ3.notes: Lumenpioneer's own round-die 3000K thrower (2.3 mm² glowing area). Same chip as the FFL505A, but low-CRI and much more efficient. Higher luminance than the FFL505A and XP-L HI. Lab: 3208K, Duv +0.0015, turning redder as current rises. One Convoy buyer reported ~84 CRI, which the lab didn't reproduce. BLF rates it weaker than the 3000K SFT-40.

W5050SQ5.title: LMP W5050SQ5
W5050SQ5.notes: Higher-current round-die thrower (4000K/5000K); tint close to the LHP531.

LML2AW.title: LML2AW
LML2AW.notes: Budget 3000K/4000K drop-in replacement for the SST-40. Users report better tint than the SST-40, though batches vary.

YinDing 5050 Glass.title: YinDing 5050 Glass (95 CRI)
YinDing 5050 Glass.notes: Round die under an AR glass cap with a near-on-BBL tint and a clean beam in reflectors and TIRs — essentially no direct competitor in cold-white high-CRI. Same chip family as the W5050SQ3/FFL505A round-die parts and likely San'an-made. Batch lottery: an earlier ~5500–6000K 70-CRI glass sample measured very green with high Vf, and AliExpress supply is unreliable.

FC40.title: Getian GT-FC40
FC40.notes: 16-die domeless "waffle" emitter (as warm as 1800K). Throws more than a domed XHP70 but has been outcompeted by XHP70.3 HI and FFL707A. Extended-CRI tops at R9050, not R9080 — a correction on the BLF guide thread itself.

SST-10 IR.title: Luminus SST-10-IR
SST-10 IR.notes: Night-vision/covert IR. 850 nm shows a faint red glow; 940 nm is effectively invisible but works less well with most cameras.

XP-E.title: Cree XP-E2 (colour)
XP-E.notes: Long-standing standard for coloured channels in multi-channel builds.

LH351D.title: Samsung LH351D
LH351D.notes: Samsung bins run 2700K–6500K. Cheap and floody with a big dome; available in cool-white high CRI. Tends green (nicknamed "dogfarts") and bins vary. Superseded by 519A but still a decent budget pick.

TN-3535.title: LatticePower TN3535
TN-3535.output: 1,050 lm @ 3 A (90 CRI, lab) · ~1,970 lm (90 CRI) / ~3,100 lm (70 CRI) at max overdrive (lab, 25 °C)
TN-3535.notes: Domed single-die flip chip, similar to the LH351D. The big 8.4 mm² source makes it a flood LED, not a thrower. The 90 CRI sample measured Ra 94 / R9 71 but had a green tint (Duv +0.0055), and the 70 CRI bins have R9 below −25. Vf goes past 4 V at max current, so avoid direct drive. Found in budget Sofirn and Wurkkos lights (e.g. Sofirn SR23 / ST10, early Wurkkos TS26).

CSP2323.title: LatticePower CSP2323
CSP2323.notes: 4000K or 6000K in Wurkkos lights. Tiny CSP, brighter than the E21A with slightly worse colour. Popular in small triples such as the Wurkkos TS10.

HL2X.title: Lumileds HL2X
HL2X.notes: Domed with decent colour; notable 1800K 80 CRI version.

UHi.title: NiteLab UHi 20 / UHi 40
UHi.notes: Cool white only: 5600–6600K measured in an EDC27 UHi, with a green (positive-Duv) tint. Nitecore's in-house emitters (Sysmax). Very high output but very low CRI; found in many current Nitecore lights.

SST-25.title: SST-25
SST-25.notes: Domed cool-white flood emitter. Mostly seen in Fenix lights: four in the C7 PRO, eight in the LR35R PRO, twelve in the LR36R and two in the HM75R PRO.

XHP50.3 HD.title: XHP50.3 HD
XHP50.3 HD.notes: The high-density sibling of the XHP50.3 HI: Cree rates it for lumens rather than throw, so expect a wider, less intense hotspot. Found in the Fenix TK17.

SL-F50S.title: Skilhunt SL-F50S
SL-F50S.notes: Skilhunt's own quad-die flip-chip LED, 5000K high CRI. Efficacy is close to the FFL5009R and XHP50.3 HI, but the larger die throws less in the same optic. No datasheet and not sold bare; only in Skilhunt lights such as the H300 and M300 V4.

HL4X.title: Lumileds HL4X
HL4X.notes: LUXEON HL4X, the bigger sibling of the HL2X. Eight of them give the Acebeam X20-R its 10,000 lm / 440 m (vs 8,000 lm / 645 m with SFT-25R). No public datasheet found.

XP-G4.title: XP-G4 / XP-L2
XP-G4.notes: Both 2700K–7000K. Efficient and very common in mainstream brands (Fenix, Olight, etc.). Domed, with poor colour and noticeable tint shift; enthusiasts generally avoid them.

XP-L2.title: XP-G4 / XP-L2
XP-L2.notes: Both 2700K–7000K. Efficient and very common in mainstream brands (Fenix, Olight, etc.). Domed, with poor colour and noticeable tint shift; enthusiasts generally avoid them.

XP-LR.title: XP-GR / XP-LR / XM-MR / XFLMNR
XP-LR.notes: 5000K, 5700K or 6500K only (Cree). Cree's newer round-die (round LES) throw parts, with source sizes of 1.3–2.8 mm. Cree's direct answer to the SFT-25R / SFT-40 class. Few enthusiast tests yet.

XP-L HD.title: XP-L HD
XP-L HD.notes: Domed high-density XP-L: floodier and slightly brighter than the domeless XP-L HI. Older but still in budget lights.

XP-L.title: XP-L HD
XP-L.notes: Domed high-density XP-L: floodier and slightly brighter than the domeless XP-L HI. Older but still in budget lights.

SST-12.title: SST-12
SST-12.notes: Domed small round-die emitter in the XP footprint, a step down from the SST-20 with a tidier beam. Max 1.8 A rated.

XHP50B.title: XHP50.2 / XHP70.2
XHP50B.notes: ANSI bins 3000K–7000K, EasyWhite 2700K–5000K. Older domed XHP generation: very bright but floody, with visible rainbow tint shift. Still sold by Convoy.

GT-FC40.title: Getian GT-FC40
GT-FC40.notes: 16-die domeless "waffle" emitter (as warm as 1800K). Throws more than a domed XHP70 but has been outcompeted by XHP70.3 HI and FFL707A. Extended-CRI tops at R9050, not R9080 — a correction on the BLF guide thread itself.

SST-10-IR.title: Luminus SST-10-IR
SST-10-IR.notes: Night-vision/covert IR. 850 nm shows a faint red glow; 940 nm is effectively invisible but works less well with most cameras.

XP-E2.title: Cree XP-E2 (colour)
XP-E2.notes: Long-standing standard for coloured channels in multi-channel builds.

SBT-10X-UV.title: SBT-10X-UV
SBT-10X-UV.notes: ~1.3–1.4 W radiant @ 1 A (Vf ~3.8–3.9 V), pushed to ~3 A in high-power builds.

NV1010.title: NV1010
NV1010.notes: 16 × 75 mil San'an chips; 60–80 A only with excellent cooling. Wide, clean beam; the 5000K R9080 version is praised for neutral tint. Back in stock at Convoy (Nov 2026): 6000K / 5500K R70 and 5000K / 4000K / 3000K R9080, bare or on 20 / 25 mm MCPCB.

NVSU233B(T).title: NVSU233B(T)
NVSU233B(T).notes: Convoy's premium UV option; clean 365 nm output with minimal visible purple.

CUN66A1B.title: CUN66A1B
CUN66A1B.notes: Seoul Viosys UV Z5, 365–367 nm, about 1 W radiant at up to 500 mA. The UV in the Skilhunt EC200S Mini UV; sold bare at Convoy.

CUN66A1G.title: CUN66A1G
CUN66A1G.notes: High-power UV Z5 version: about 1.8 W radiant at 365–367 nm. Sold bare at Convoy.
